title: Module 1 Interpretation Check
intro: Each item gives you a short research situation. Decide what the evidence supports.

items.q: Researchers survey 300 volunteers who responded to a flyer in a gym about exercise habits. A reporter concludes that most adults exercise regularly. The main problem is
o: The volunteer sample may not represent all adults, so the statistic may miss the parameter
Exercise is measured on a nominal scale
items.why: Gym volunteers are likely more active than the general population. A biased sample produces error that a larger sample would not fix.

items.q: Students who sleep more tend to have higher GPAs in a survey. Which conclusion is justified?
o: Sleep and GPA are related in this sample, but the survey cannot show that sleep raises GPA
items.why: A survey is correlational. Both causal directions and third variables remain possible.

items.q: Participants are randomly assigned to practice a task for 10 or 30 minutes, then tested. Which conclusion is justified if the 30-minute group scores higher?
o: Longer practice caused better performance, subject to sampling error
The groups must have differed in motivation
items.why: Random assignment makes the groups equivalent on average before treatment, which supports a causal claim.

items.q: In a class of 400 students, 40 are chosen at random and their mean exam score is 78. The class mean is 80. This 2 point gap is
items.why: Random samples differ from the population by chance. A small gap like this is exactly what sampling error looks like.

items.q: A study records each participant's diagnosis (depression, anxiety, none). Which graph and summary fit this variable?
o: A bar graph and the mode
A line graph and the median
items.why: Nominal categories are summarized with counts or proportions and the mode. A mean of diagnoses has no meaning.
